comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Independent reproduction — and it is NOT limited to `search`

Reproduced live at 2026-09-06 ~01:50 UTC, with a different call type than the one on record. The
ticket's context describes 46 concurrent **`search`** calls cancelled at the client, after which a
single later `search` went unserved and died at `timed out awaiting tools/call after 300s`. I hit
the same terminal state from a **single, non-search, WRITE** call.

Sequence, in order:

1. `transition_ticket(0cfc-e511-8f8a-4c8b, in_progress -> closed)` — a close, so it runs the
   completion-verifier gate. The client aborted it: *"sent no response or progress for 300s"*.
   **The server was not stopped by that abort** — only the client gave up.
2. Immediately after, `summary([6 ticket ids])` — a trivial read — exceeded 120s and was still
   unserved.
3. I cancelled (2), which per this ticket's own thesis may itself starve the next reader.

So the starvation is reachable from **one** in-flight call, not only from a 46-way concurrent batch,
and the poisoning call need not be a `search` — it can be a long-running gated **write**. That
matters for the fix: a remedy scoped to `search`, or one keyed on concurrency count, would not have
prevented this.

### Host conditions at the time (context, not cause)

```
free -m:  total 7813   available 2615  (33.5%)
uptime:   load average 4.69, 4.99, 5.08     <-- 2-vCPU box, ~2.5x oversubscribed
docker:   rebar-mcp  2.872GiB / 7.631GiB  (37.6%, and the 7.631GiB denominator means NO mem_limit)
```

The box was under real pressure, so contention plausibly widens the window. But pressure alone does
not explain a **read** remaining unserved for 120s+ while the process is alive and healthy — that is
the queueing/serialisation defect this ticket is about.

### Probable amplifier worth checking together

Bug `lousy-unsuited-gnu` (p1) reports that resolving a single ticket id scans the whole store at
roughly 8,900 JSON parses. If that is accurate, every tracker call — including the cheap-looking
`summary` above — carries a full-store scan, which would make the serialisation window enormous and
make this starvation far easier to trigger. These two are worth reading together; fixing the scan
may substantially shrink this bug's blast radius without addressing its root cause, so do not let a
perf fix be mistaken for a fix to this.

### Operational note

While this holds, the project's documented guidance to route tracker operations through the MCP
server is effectively unavailable: the close had to fall back to the local CLI. Worth stating in the
fix that a client-side timeout **leaves the server-side operation running**, because the natural
recovery — re-firing the call — risks a duplicate, billable gate run. I did not re-fire; I verified
via the local CLI that the ticket was still `in_progress` with only a `plan-review` attestation and
no `completion-verifier`, which is how I established the close had not landed.

compiled_state.description:
## Context
A batch of 46 concurrent `search` calls was canceled at the client. A subsequent single `search` remained unserved and failed with `timed out awaiting tools/call after 300s`. The canceled calls were read-only.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Canceled or abandoned searches cannot monopolize MCP request capacity.
- [x] A later single tracker read obtains MCP worker capacity before the abandoned canceled searches finish (so it is no longer queued until the 300s tools/call deadline).
- [x] A regression test covers cancellation/backpressure for concurrent searches.

## Root Cause

The MCP server offloads synchronous tool bodies through `anyio.to_thread.run_sync` with its default `abandon_on_cancel=False` behavior. When a client cancels a long-running tool call, the request coroutine keeps waiting for the worker thread and continues holding the default thread-limiter token until the synchronous body finishes. A burst of canceled long searches can therefore occupy every worker slot, leaving a later simple read queued behind abandoned work until the client-side `tools/call` deadline expires.

## Plan

- Add a deterministic regression test that constrains the AnyIO worker limiter to one token, cancels a blocked MCP tool call, and proves a later quick tool call can still obtain request capacity before the abandoned worker finishes.
- Change the MCP sync-tool offload wrapper so client-side cancellation uses AnyIO `abandon_on_cancel=True`. A live probe on the pinned AnyIO in this worktree observed the default limiter behavior directly: with one token, `abandon_on_cancel=False` leaves `borrowed_tokens=1` and a later quick `run_sync` times out while the abandoned body is still blocked; `abandon_on_cancel=True` makes the canceled request task exit, `borrowed_tokens=0`, and the later quick call obtains capacity before the abandoned body is released.
- The failure-disposition contract is caller-gone discard: if an abandoned synchronous body later returns or raises, AnyIO intentionally ignores that result because the MCP client has already canceled. That is acceptable for current MCP tool semantics because the alternative is keeping the request slot pinned past the client deadline; mutating tools already rely on idempotent tracker operations and expose persistence/readback separately.
- Keep certified-tool gauge instrumentation intact and do not add new store locks or search-specific throttles. Add regression coverage for gauge cleanup after the abandoned certified body eventually exits so there is no gauge leak or double decrement.

## Testing

- RED: run the new targeted regression test before the implementation and confirm it fails on current `origin/main`.
- GREEN: run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/unit/test_mcp_tool_offload.py -q`.
- Run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`.
- Before push, run `env -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT -u GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0 -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 -u GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1 -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1 -u GIT_CONFIG_KEY_2 -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_2 PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make verify` and, if the known repo-isolation GIT_CONFIG artifact appears, confirm the named test solo with the same env-unset prefix.

file_impact.reason: Change the MCP sync-tool offload wrapper cancellation semantics so canceled callers abandon worker results and release request capacity.
Add the regression test for canceled long-running tool calls not starving later reads.

compiled_state.title: Canceled MCP searches starve later tracker reads
